question: Should OpenClaw own static Codex model price defaults in the bundled Codex provider, or should this PR limit itself to recomputing generated zero-cost records from already configured pricing?
rationale: The stale API id is mechanical, but bundled price snapshots can change existing users' reported spend after upgrade and need maintainer ownership of the pricing source.

options.title: Keep resolver-only fix
options.body: Rebase the zero-cost resolver and tests onto current main, preserve `openai-chatgpt-responses`, and omit bundled static Codex prices unless accepted separately.

options.title: Accept static Codex pricing
options.body: Merge the price defaults and fallback model only if maintainers explicitly own the price-source and upgrade-visible reporting behavior.

options.title: Close for a fresh PR
options.body: If no one wants to repair this stale branch, close it and invite a narrow current-main PR with the useful accounting fix.

recommendation.title: Keep resolver-only fix
recommendation.body: Rebase the zero-cost resolver and tests onto current main, preserve `openai-chatgpt-responses`, and omit bundled static Codex prices unless accepted separately.

likelyOwner.reason: This decision sits at the Codex provider/OpenAI unification boundary where recent history points most strongly to steipete.
